Subject: Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant Application - Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC)

Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC) is a proud minority-owned social enterprise committed to tackling the urgent need for gun safety education within Sacramento's communities of color. Our vital mission is to prevent preventable gun-related accidents and foster responsible firearm ownership through culturally relevant, engaging, and innovative programs.

The alarming rates of accidental shootings and gun violence disproportionately impact our neighborhoods, creating an imperative for accessible, practical safety knowledge. GAFC, in strong partnership with the esteemed Church of Legacy, directly addresses this need. Our multi-faceted approach includes developing the "Gloxsie 21" cartoon IP, specifically crafted to teach crucial safety concepts to youth in an engaging way; hands-on community workshops covering safe storage, handling, and conflict de-escalation; and AI education initiatives that not only embed safety messaging but also empower residents with valuable 21st-century technological literacy.

Funding from the Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant will allow GAFC to significantly expand our outreach, leading to tangible outcomes: a measurable reduction in accidental gun incidents, a dramatic increase in responsible firearm practices across households, and the empowerment of youth with life-saving knowledge and future-ready skills. As a minority-owned organization deeply rooted in Sacramento, GAFC offers unparalleled cultural competency and established trust within the communities we serve, ensuring our education is both effective and resonant. Our unique blend of innovation, community partnership, and direct lived experience makes us exceptionally qualified.

We respectfully request $15,000 from the Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant to amplify our programs and cultivate safer, more informed communities throughout Sacramento.
